blockMcqs.question: What does a full backup copy?
options: The entire database at a point in time
blockMcqs.explanation: A full backup copies every byte of the database, making it self-contained but large.

blockMcqs.question: A differential backup copies data changed since when?
blockMcqs.explanation: Differential always measures from the last full backup, so restore only needs full + one differential.

blockMcqs.question: What enables point-in-time recovery beyond the last backup?
options: A second full backup taken mid-day
Reading the undo log in reverse
blockMcqs.explanation: WAL records every change; PITR restores the last backup and replays WAL up to the target timestamp.

blockMcqs.question: RPO of 30 minutes means you must back up at least every…
blockMcqs.explanation: RPO is the maximum data loss you can afford; to guarantee ≤30 min loss you must capture a backup every 30 minutes.

blockMcqs.question: A hot standby differs from a warm standby because it…
options: Is kept fully in sync with the primary
Can take traffic immediately without delay
blockMcqs.explanation: A hot standby is ready to serve traffic the moment failover is triggered; a warm standby needs time to start accepting connections.

blockMcqs.question: High replication lag on a replica primarily means…
options: The primary is running out of connections
The replica is serving stale reads and has a larger recovery gap
Disk usage on the primary is critically low
Slow queries are blocking WAL writes
blockMcqs.explanation: Lag means the replica is behind — reads are stale and if failover happens now there is more data to replay or potentially lose.

blockMcqs.question: Fetching 50 orders then one query per order's customer is an example of…
blockMcqs.explanation: 1 query for orders + 50 queries for customers = 51 queries. The fix is eager loading to join in one query.

blockMcqs.question: Why should new columns be added nullable first in production migrations?
options: Nullable columns are faster to index
Old app code still runs without supplying the new column
The ORM requires nullable columns for mapping
It reduces WAL size during the migration
blockMcqs.explanation: Adding NOT NULL immediately fails old code that doesn't supply the value; nullable first allows a safe zero-downtime rollout.
